article_hits.content: Burnham's push for closer EU ties causes ripples in his party and others Image source, EPA/Shutterstock By Harry Farley , Political correspondent , Henry Zeffman , Chief political correspondent and Jack Fenwick , Political correspondent Published 24 minutes ago There is renewed attention on the prime minister's push for closer relations with Europe - and that is causing ripples in his own party and others. Andy Burnham told his Cabinet earlier this week: "I firmly believe we have ended up with a harder Brexit than people voted for… no sensible person thinks the deal negotiated by the Tories is working for the country." It comes ahead of a week which will focus minds on the UK's relationship with the bloc. On Thursday, at a gathering of European leaders in Dublin, Burnham will for the first time meet those who could prove pivotal as he sells his vision for Britain's future in the bloc. article_hits.content: Clashes in Barcelona as thousands join Spain general strike Image source, Reuters By Nick Beake , Europe correspondent , Reporting from Madrid , Guy Hedgecoe , Reporting from Madrid and Alba Morgade Published 11 November 2026, 14:06 GMT Updated 24 minutes ago Clashes have broken out between groups of protesters and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living. Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas. Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption. Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November.
